parsed.rationale: Three distinct types — `HSBColor` in the `ColorPalette` package and `AccentColor` and `HSBOffset` in the `Wallpaper` package — each independently define an identical `init(hue:saturation:brightness:)` initializer. Because the types are semantically related (all represent HSB colour concepts) but are not in an inheritance hierarchy, the most idiomatic Swift remedy is to introduce a protocol `HSBInitializable` with a required `init(hue:saturation:brightness:)` and provide a default implementation in a protocol extension, eliminating the three duplicate bodies. The protocol should live in `Shared/ColorPalette/Sources/ColorPalette/` since `ColorPalette` is already the canonical HSB package and `Wallpaper` already depends on it (evidenced by `HSBColor` being defined there while `Wallpaper` defines its own HSB-shaped types).
